name: wild-willows
author: Bailey Dunning
description: Wild Willows — a cozy nature-restoration life sim

scripts.build: npm run build:server && npm run build:web
scripts.i18n:test: vitest run --project unit tests/unit/i18n.test.ts tests/unit/i18n-es.test.ts tests/unit/simple-text.test.ts
scripts.test:integration: npm run build:server && vitest run --project integration
scripts.test:all: npm run check && npm run test && npm run test:e2e:solo
scripts.android:init: npm i -D @capacitor/core@latest @capacitor/cli@latest @capacitor/android@latest @capacitor/filesystem@latest && npx cap add android && node scripts/patch-android.mjs
scripts.android:sync: npm run build:web && npx cap sync android && node scripts/patch-android.mjs
scripts.android:apk: npm run android:sync && cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease
scripts.android:aab: npm run android:sync && cd android && ./gradlew bundleRelease

androidComment: Android/ChromeOS build (Capacitor). Run `npm run android:init` ONCE to install Capacitor, scaffold android/, and apply the ChromeOS patches; after that `npm run android:apk` (itch) or `npm run android:aab` (Play) is the whole loop. The android/ directory is generated and gitignored — scripts/patch-android.mjs re-applies every setting we care about and is idempotent, so a regenerated tree is never a lossy one. IMPORTANT: the @capacitor/* packages are devDependencies ON PURPOSE. Vite bundles @capacitor/core and @capacitor/filesystem into web/ at build time, so nothing needs them at runtime — and electron-builder auto-packages production `dependencies`, so listing them there would push Capacitor into every desktop/Steam build for no reason. Signing is env-driven (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PATH / _PASSWORD / ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS / ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD); with none set, Gradle falls back to debug signing so a local smoke build still works.
masComment: Mac App Store variant (`npm run desktop:mas`). Inherits `mac` config, so everything notarized-DMG-specific is overridden here: MAS uses the App Sandbox instead of the hardened runtime + notarization, its own entitlements pair, and a provisioning profile from developer.apple.com (put it at build/embedded.provisionprofile — gitignored; CI decodes it from a secret). steamworks.js is excluded: Steam can't run inside the MAS sandbox and electron/steam.js already no-ops when the module is missing. ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=false answers App Store Connect's export-compliance question (HTTPS only). NOTE (electron-builder 26+): mac.notarize is now a boolean — the notary team ID JB4CT3MZ6L moved to the APPLE_TEAM_ID env var, which CI must set alongside APPLE_ID and APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD.
comment: v1 ships SOLO-ONLY on itch.io: solo runs the game logic in-app against local save files (fully offline), so the desktop app needs no server and no network. `steamworks.js` is the only runtime dependency electron-builder must package (native, desktop-only, asarUnpacked). `harper` is a DEV-ONLY tool now (local web dev via `harper dev .`, and the co-op E2E harness) — it is intentionally NOT a production dependency so electron-builder doesn't bundle its heavy/native tree into every platform's app (which also de-risks the cross-platform CI builds). Co-op (hosted Harper) is hidden behind COOP_ENABLED in src/features.ts; flip it on and move `harper` back to `dependencies` if you ship co-op.
